item.text: {"question_id":"6B.2","answer":"For 2023, the evidence supports government-backed efforts to expand access, but not a demonstrated broad improvement in affordable, effective uptake across essential services. Free primary education was associated with more than 3.6 million additional public-primary enrollments in 2021–2022, and a separate government report states that enrollment reached about four million in 2022; these figures predate or only contextualize 2023 and do not establish attendance, affordability, quality, completion, or equitable access (BATCH-0014-E004; BATCH-0012-R01-E019). In 2023, the government pursued free primary education, universal health coverage, free maternity and newborn care, family planning, displaced-children schooling, and the PDL-145T; the presidential monitoring structure acknowledged implementation difficulties, and the PDL-145T evidence records construction launches and projected deliveries rather than completed or taken-up services (BATCH-0010-E006; BATCH-0020-E012; BATCH-0023-E001). Programme evidence indicates some WASH, food-security, and livelihood improvements, but these were delivered through a WFP-, UNICEF-, and FAO-led programme with only 50% of planned activities fully implemented, generally low access to improved water and sanitation, and no president-specific or national causal estimate (BATCH-0002-E001; BATCH-0002-E002; BATCH-0002-E003). Conditions remained severely constrained: nearly seven million children were out of school, more than 2,000 schools had closed in conflict-affected eastern provinces, health systems were at a breaking point for millions needing assistance, and maternal and newborn access was exceptionally difficult (BATCH-0022-E010; BATCH-0003-E013; BATCH-0008-E002). Implementation reliability was further weakened when the government dissolved the Social Fund and disbursements for three World Bank-financed projects were paused during transition arrangements; later parliamentary and Court of Accounts criticisms also reported weak provincial allocations, irregular spending, uncertified debts, and works described in the budget without observed field action (BATCH-0017-E002; BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0024-E004). Overall, the record shows attributable policy commitments and some partial delivery, especially in education and planned local infrastructure, but insufficient evidence of broad, affordable, effective, and equitable access or uptake across the service
